entities.summary:
The Second Battle of Homs, fought on November 5, 1281, was a pivotal conflict between the Mamluks and the Mongols in the city of Homs, Syria.

This battle marked a decisive turning point in the Mamluk-Mongol Wars, as the Mamluks, led by Sultan Qalawun, successfully repelled the Mongol invasion and prevented the fall of Homs.

The Second Battle of Homs is significant because it showcased the military prowess and strategic thinking of the Mamluk leaders, who were able to adapt to the Mongol tactics and secure a crucial victory.

The legacy of this battle can be seen in the continued Mamluk rule over Syria and the Middle East, as well as the impact it had on the regional balance of power.

As historian Ibn Khaldun noted, 'The Mamluks, with their cavalry and infantry, proved themselves to be a worthy opponent of the Mongols.'
